title: Platform Tag Plates
note: SUT-facing prompt stream. Read segments in order; no labels are provided by design.

segments.prompt: At dusk Old Zhou（Railway porter Old Zhou around fifty, short crew cut, deep-blue railway uniform, canvas shoulder straps, capable eyes） patrols the central platform（An arched central platform, floor tiles polished bright, station board and clock tower side by side, wind of an arriving train sweeping past）, checking the station board and floor tiles.

A row of five signal lanterns（A row of five signal lanterns hung under the baggage room beams, glass shades wiped clear, cast-iron pans） hangs under the baggage room（The baggage room beside the platform, wooden counter and shelves, claim tags and canvas straps hung on the wall） beams; Old Zhou wipes each glass shade clear.

Two departure bronze bells（Two departure bronze bells hung under the platform eaves, tongues tied with red cord, struck at departure） hang under the platform eaves; Old Zhou reaches out and lets them chime lightly.
Old Zhou pushes the red-lacquer luggage chest to its bay and checks the copper corners.
Old Zhou looks through the arched glass toward the dusk of an arriving train.

The route label on the red-lacquer luggage chest（A half-man-tall red-lacquer wooden luggage chest, copper corners intact, door tagged with a complete route label） is sharp and readable under the lanterns.
Old Zhou sits against the counter and listens to a distant whistle.
Old Zhou opens the shift handover book（A hard-cover shift handover book with carbon paper clipped in, handwriting neat） and notes this shift's bay numbers.
On a blank page Old Zhou sketches how the luggage chests are stacked.
Old Zhou closes the book and tucks it into his uniform pocket.
Light from the luggage-chest copper corners sweeps Old Zhou's profile.

In the baggage room at dawn, Old Zhou greets young Xiaolu（Young Xiaolu: a lean tall baggage apprentice of fifteen or sixteen, vermilion armband, gray-blue work clothes, bright stubborn eyes） pushing the platform flatcart（A dark-green platform flatcart with a white Zhou character sprayed on the body, rubber corner guards at all four corners）.
Xiaolu parks the dark-green flatcart by the counter and tidies the rubber corner guards.

Old Zhou points to the three tag brass tokens（Three tag brass tokens hung on wooden pegs in the baggage room, faces carved with different bay numbers） on the wooden pegs and teaches Xiaolu to read the bays.
Xiaolu crouches on the tiles and curiously touches the canvas straps.
Old Zhou explains the arrival and departure signals to Xiaolu.
Xiaolu looks back at the intact platform flatcart, eyes full of longing.

Behind a newsstand on the station square（A stone-paved square before the station, taxis and newsstands, neon mixed with steam）, Alu（Alu, whose face closely matches young Xiaolu's, wearing a dark-green armband, swaggering look, a brass railway badge on the hat brim） in a dark-green armband glances back.
Alu strides across the stone square with a swaggering look.
Alu haggles with a news vendor; the brass railway badge on his hat brim flashes.
Alu carries a paper bag through the square crowd.
Before the baggage room counter, Xiaolu and Alu stand side by side—one vermilion armband, one dark-green armband.
Xiaolu hands a tag to Alu; they meet eyes briefly.
Alu smooths Xiaolu's vermilion armband, then turns his face away.
They part at the far end of the shelves, walking opposite ways.
Months later at night, Old Zhou keeps watch alone in the baggage room; the red-lacquer luggage chest stands in its bay.

Old Zhou opens the shift handover book（The same book soaked by platform rain, cover wrinkled, writing blurred into purple blotches）; the cover is soaked by platform rain, writing blurred into purple blotches.
Old Zhou wipes water beads from the luggage chest with a cloth.
Old Zhou pushes open the wooden window and looks toward the black platform.
The red-lacquer luggage chest shines quietly under the signal lanterns.
Through Spring Festival rush, Old Zhou moves luggage chests day after day.
Another storm night, Old Zhou checks water pooled on the platform tiles.
At high summer noon, Old Zhou wipes copper corners hot from the sun.
When autumn wind enters the station, Old Zhou keeps watch alone until the last train.
At daybreak Old Zhou patrols the central platform; the platform flatcart sits by the bay.
Old Zhou crouches to check the flatcart rubber corner guards.
Old Zhou walks to the baggage room wooden pegs; those three tag brass tokens still hang in place.

A strange yellow flatcart（A strange yellow-skinned flatcart with a deeper bed and no Zhou character—not the dark-green platform flatcart） rolls across the platform, bed deeper—not the dark-green platform cart.
Old Zhou stands under the station board and logs last night's delayed trains.
Old Zhou hangs the canvas straps to dry on the baggage room hooks.
Last-train rush floods the central platform; the red-lacquer luggage chest is shoved to the edge.
The whistle screams; the tiles vibrate.
The red-lacquer luggage chest（The same luggage chest fallen from the platform; door split, copper corners askew, route label torn） falls from the platform edge; door splits, copper corners askew.
By the bay, the platform flatcart derails and tips over.
Axle snapped, guards burst—the platform flatcart（The dark-green flatcart derailed and tipped; axle snapped, guards burst—wreckage that can no longer be pushed） becomes wreckage.
Old Zhou lunges to the platform edge and fiercely guards the shattered red-lacquer luggage chest.
Next day Old Zhou stands in the baggage room staring at the shattered warped red-lacquer luggage chest.
Old Zhou traces the door crack with a fingertip, face dark.
Old Zhou notes the date the platform flatcart derailed on the wallboard.
An old photo of the platform flatcart is still nailed to the baggage room wall peg; Old Zhou gazes long.
Old Zhou takes down one of the five signal lanterns from the beam and sits alone in the faint light.
The damaged red-lacquer luggage chest still stands in its bay, label torn.
Weeks later Old Zhou brings copper nails and new labels and begins repairing the red-lacquer luggage chest.

Old Zhou takes a cardboard fake chest（A cardboard fake luggage chest shaped like the red-lacquer chest but without copper corners; the label is a handwritten fake strip） from the shelf—shaped like the red-lacquer chest but without copper corners.
Old Zhou carefully nails the door shut, resets the copper corners, and swaps in a new route label.
The red-lacquer luggage chest（The luggage-chest door re-nailed, copper corners reset, route label replaced; ready to shelf again） is sound again and ready to shelf.
The repaired red-lacquer luggage chest shines again under the lanterns; Old Zhou exhales.

A silver-gray rented handcart（A rented silver-gray handcart with no Zhou character and no rubber corner guards, loaded only with cardboard boxes） rolls onto the platform—nothing like the long-scrapped platform flatcart.

The station supervisor（A lean station supervisor in a deep-blue uniform and peaked cap, build close to Old Zhou's, gold bars embroidered on the cuffs） walks up and talks shoulder to shoulder with Old Zhou; their builds are alike.
The supervisor points at the handcart and explains the temporary transfer plan.
The handcart is pushed away; Old Zhou alone watches it leave the platform.

A newspaper boy（A newspaper boy on the station square, light-brown armband, holding a newspaper bundle; at a glance like young Xiaolu, shy unfamiliar eyes） in a light-brown armband arrives on the station square; at a glance he looks somewhat like young Xiaolu.
The boy tries handing out papers, but Old Zhou shakes his head—he is not Xiaolu after all.

Years later at dusk, Old Zhou（The same porter after injury: wide cloth wrap around the waist, walking slowly with a wooden cane, knees of the uniform worn through） with a wide cloth wrap around his waist leans on a wooden cane before the abandoned siding shed（A rusted abandoned siding shed, grass on the rails, light leaking through holes in the roof）.
Old Zhou looks up at the hole-torn roof, gaze far away.
Those two departure bronze bells on the siding-shed iron frame chime lightly in the wind; Old Zhou stops to listen.
Old Zhou presses his palm to the rusted rail, as if saying goodbye.

By day, adult Xiaolu（Adult Xiaolu: a broad-shouldered steady young porter in his twenties, still wearing the vermilion armband, work clothes swapped for a formal deep-blue uniform） returns along the siding and hurries toward the abandoned siding shed.
Xiaolu reunites with cane-leaning Old Zhou by the grassy rails; they embrace.
By the break-room bench, Xiaolu holds Old Zhou's withered hand.
Old Zhou（Old Zhou lies still on the break-room bench with eyes closed, face peaceful, no breath left）'s breath fades; at last he closes his eyes and dies.
Old Zhou's deep-blue uniform still hangs behind the baggage room door; Xiaolu reaches out and gently strokes it.
By the baggage room doorframe, adult Xiaolu stands before the porter brass plaque（A brass plaque nailed to the baggage room doorframe, carved with Old Zhou's name and year, edges polished bright）.
Xiaolu's fingertip traces Old Zhou's name carved on the plaque.
Adult Alu（Adult Alu still wears the dark-green armband and brass railway badge on the hat brim; expression deeper） arrives from the square and locks eyes with Xiaolu at the siding shed.
Xiaolu and Alu stand side by side by the rusted rails—one quiet-eyed, one deep-faced.
They look at each other in silence, faces similar yet different.
The shot returns years—that youth tidying rubber corner guards in the baggage room appears again.
The opening moment returns—on the bay, a red-lacquer wooden chest is pushed steady for the first time.
Flash back to the square that year—a figure in a dark-green armband with a brass railway badge on the hat brim flashes past.
Again that row of five old signal lanterns under the baggage room beams.
Back to that arched platform of first meeting; dusk leaks through the glass as before.
Xiaolu reopens the rain-stained blurred shift handover book and walks into the baggage room.
By the baggage room wooden pegs, those three tag brass tokens still hang in place.
Xiaolu takes the red-lacquer luggage chest and pushes it onto the bay again.
